system.summary: Word-spaced directional i-digraph and homophonic substitution on lowercase Latin letters, digits, and looped '&' (where 'i' acts as a prefix/suffix modifier turning X into distinct Xi and iX digraphs; 43 recovered signs plus 30=che, 44 entries total), paired with two-digit codes (including 6 provisional candidate nulls) and underlined-L superscript nomenclators.

diacritics.note: Acute stroke on 'é' (homophone of 'e' = r); underlined capital 'L' with superscript numerals ({L2}, {L9}, {L30}, {L36}) for proper-noun nomenclators; flanking dots on some two-digit groups (.23., .27., .31., .46.).

system.doubled_letters: special sign (zo=tt, zz=zz, iz=gg, ig=ss, medial ib=nn)

solution.what: Live DECODE sweeps (Federico, Ferrante, Mantova), Cryptiana, cyphersolver_repo keys, and 16 adjacent Modena Estense Campori Federico II letters (sfasc. I-II, all clear) confirmed no surviving 1536-1538 key and no prior edition online.

Stitched all 8 native IIIF canvases (cc. 12r-15v, 2976-3094 x 4088-4128 px) and produced blind diplomatic and clean transcriptions of c. 12r, c. 13r-13v (30 lines: 265 non-clear tokens; 1,459 glyph chars excluding punctuation/braces, 1,509 raw non-space chars), and c. 15v; verified c. 14r gutter overlap.

Monoalphabetic and plain homophonic substitution hypotheses failed; character distribution (i = 29.7% of cipher characters) revealed a directional i-digraph modifier architecture (X vs Xi vs iX) paired with doubled-letter digraphs (zo=tt, zz=zz, iz=gg, ig=ss, ib=e/nn) and 30=che.

Recovered 43 directional digraph and singleton values (21 digraphs + 22 singletons) plus 30=che (44 entries total) using inline clear Italian passages (e.g., L04 considerando next to ri34=sia) together with ciphertext-side analysis, decoding connected 1537 Italian on both recto (c. 13r) and verso (c. 13v) referencing il vescovo de Casale / dela Barba, el Speciano, Il Iovio, Milan, and the fortress of Hesdin (Edim).

Strict zero-choice 1-value deterministic key test on the fitted key (validate_2162.py, zero silent drops, zero target lexicon boosts, ig=g removed): 230 letter-words (964 sign tokens) LM/char -2.1500 (z=+9.37 vs 200 shuffled keys, z=+43.14 vs 200 shuffled streams; exact IT_WORDS hit 182/230 = 79.1%, len>=4 86/121 = 71.1%, z=+46.40 / +47.04); leak-free rossi1537/reading_A.md prose-word synthetic control 207/212 (97.6%) exact words, 965/979 (98.6%) chars; negative controls FAIL (exit=1) on all-'e' and all-'a' constant keys.

Pre-PR adversarial audits (OpenAI Codex gpt-6.2-astra, 19 Nov and 26 Nov 2026) verified the Estense IIIF manifest and live tile match (MAD < 1 RGB level), ran zero-lexicon recto-to-verso transfer (11 retrospectively selected recto words -> 28 signs -> verso L25-L30), removed disputed ig=g in favor of passati (L18) and fussi (L12), corrected Hesdin capture date to 13-14 April 1537 and Bernardino Castellari's death date to 27 June 1546, fixed the rossi1537 synthetic control to read segmented prose from reading_A.md, aligned outcome.method to adjacent plaintext, and flagged L04-L06 and L19 for explicit brackets.

Unedited full-coverage mechanical decryption (decryption_13r_13v.txt) and strict cipher-words-only reading audit (word_audit_2162.py & v10_relabel.py, clear_markup=⟨⟩): 219/267 sure cipher words (0.820, 48 holes: 13 open proper-noun nomenclators, 9 open two-digit codes/provisional candidate nulls, 9 uncertain/contextual words, 17 scribal slips) -> read in part.

Integration review of PR #1019 (AI agent, for the maintainers): an independent tiler over key_gonzaga1537.tsv reproduced decryption_13r_13v.txt on all 30 lines with the same 43 ambiguous parses; sure words recounted 219/267 (0.820); c. 13r L01-L07 compared with the Estense IIIF image and matched, except L02/L03 lizh, which the leaf shows as li3b (already bracketed [più], count unchanged, added to Transcription doubts). Gap blockers set to one outside type each. Not checked: c. 13r L08-L24 and c. 13v against the image, the validation figures, the Potter and DBI citations.

Write-up escalation check (AI agent): c. 13r compared with the Estense IIIF canvas at 1400 px and full-size crops. L02/L03 show li3b, which the key decodes as pio (period form of più), so those two holes are workable; L04 'uiro e' may be clear Italian 'uero è' rather than cipher; c. 13r L08-L24 and c. 13v still not compared with the image. Write-up held, Status set to in progress pending a transcription re-check.

Image re-check (AI model, Claude, for the maintainers; not blind, no person): c. 13r L01-L24 and c. 13v L25-L30 compared line by line with the full-size Estense IIIF canvases (nine 1500-px regions each, stitched), with close crops of the 17 bracketed slips and the flagged places. 12 corrections written as a separate layer (recheck/corrections.tsv, recheck/transcription_13r_13v_recheck.txt; the contributor's files unchanged): L02/L03 lizh->li3b (pio), L04 uiro e->clear uero e, L05 fiirsibp 4->fiirsibpi4, L10 gg->9 (demostrato), L11 ei->ti (quele), L13 d->é (respetto), L16 +->4 (Al), L19 ri,->r, (è), L23 omitted c restored (essendo), L27 t->l twice (peggiore; posse still a hole). His decoder and key re-run unchanged (recheck/decryption_13r_13v_recheck.txt). Read share by the README rule (v10_relabel, clear_markup ⟨⟩): before 219 sure / 48 holes / 267 = 0.820; after 221 sure / 46 holes / 267 = 0.828, with 10 of the holes probable (AI-settled look-alike signs; 0.865 if granted). The other 14 doubtful words show on the scan as transcribed (writer's slips or unvalued shapes), and the 22 open codes have no key sheet or sibling online.

texts.label: c. 13r-13v (catalogue 2162, Piedmont intelligence enclosure in Federico II Gonzaga's letter of 6 May 1537)
texts.summary: A two-section secret Piedmont intelligence sheet copied in Mantua and enclosed in Federico II Gonzaga's 6 May 1537 letter to Ferrante Gonzaga: Section 1 criticises an unnamed figure [46] for reckless, vain conduct and notes that the Bishop of Casale (contextually Bernardino Castellari, called della Barba) is held under suspicion through Speciano (contextually Giovanni Battista Speciano); Section 2 reports troops passing over to {L2?} with banners unfurled, the surrender of the fortress of Hesdin (Edim, 13-14 April 1537), Giovio's (contextually Paolo Giovio's) warning to {L30?}, and public opinion in Milan that {L30?} stands in the worst possible credit.

outcome.notes: Substantially deciphered using inline clear Italian passages plus ciphertext-side cryptanalysis (43 signs + 30=che; 219/267 = 82.0% sure cipher words under key_gonzaga1537.tsv, clear_markup=⟨⟩, 48 holes -> partial extent under the 95% threshold). No surviving key sheet or contemporary decipherment.
